cmo-cmo-2020-04.prompt: Let $S = \{1, 4, 8, 9, 16, \dots\}$ be the set of perfect powers of integers, i.e. numbers of the form $n^k$ where $n, k$ are positive integers and $k \ge 2$. Write $S = \{a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots\}$ with terms in increasing order, so that $a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < \cdots$. Prove that there exist infinitely many integers $m$ such that $9999$ divides the difference $a_{m+1} - a_m$.
cmo-cmo-2020-04.answer: Take consecutive squares $x^2, (x+1)^2$ with $x \equiv 4999 \pmod{9999}$, so the gap $2x+1$ is divisible by $9999$. If from some point on every such gap contained a non-square perfect power (an odd power $b^e$, $e \ge 3$), there would be $\gg \sqrt n$ such powers up to $n$, but there are at most $n^{1/3}\log_2 n$.

cmo-cmo-2020-05.prompt: There are $19\,998$ people on a social media platform, where any pair of them may or may not be friends. For any group of $9\,999$ people, there are at least $9\,999$ pairs of them that are friends. What is the least number of friendships, that is, the least number of pairs of people that are friends, that must be among the $19\,998$ people?
